packs.title: Gettysburg in the Round
packs.promise: Look closely at a work of art, a ridge and a working farm as three different ways into Gettysburg.

q.s: Let a small detail change your reading of a work.
st: Choose one work in the current exhibition. From a few steps back, give it a one-word mood.
Move closer within the allowed viewing area and look for the mark, material or edge you missed the first time.
Read the label. Save the artist’s name if given, your first word and the detail that made you keep or change it.

q.s: Find one view that opens up and another that ends quickly.
st: At one summit viewpoint, find a feature you can see far away. Note what lies between you and it.
At a second point along the open path, look for a rock, fold of ground or tree line that cuts a view short.
Finish the pair with two phrases, one beginning “I can see…” and one beginning “Hidden from here…”. For the second, name the obstruction rather than guessing what is beyond it.

q.s: Draw the part of a presidential home that feels like somebody’s house.
st: Find a public path with a clear view of the house. Choose one ordinary feature, perhaps a window or a stretch of porch.
Sketch just that part on an imaginary postcard, leaving the rest of the building out. A close description works too.
Write one line under your sketch telling someone what first made you stop there.

packs.title: Gettysburg from the Station to the Square
packs.promise: Follow a railroad arrival into town, frame York Street like a photographer and meet the people of Baltimore Street.

q.s: Give a tiny downtown moment the title of a film.
st: From the public sidewalk, look at the shape of the marquee and how its face meets the street.
Listen or look for one ordinary action nearby, such as a door swinging shut. Invent a movie title of five words or fewer about it.
Lay the title out in your notes as if it belonged on the marquee. Decide which word would get the most light.

q.s: Follow the sightline in a sculpture beside the Wills House.
st: Look at the clothes and stance of both sculpted figures. Pick one detail that places them in different times.
Follow the direction of Lincoln’s raised hat toward the house. Find where your own eye lands.
Record a pair of clues, one from the figures and one from the building.

q.s: Let a book choose where you pause on Baltimore Street.
st: Find a book that catches your eye and settle in a permitted reading spot.
Read a page, slowly enough to notice one small detail. Close the book and see what you still remember.
Jot down the title and your memory of the detail, then follow the library’s directions for returning the book.
